hs.name: ISO Harmonised Structure
hs.description: The clause structure (4 to 10) shared by every ISO management system standard.

iso9001.name: ISO 9001 Quality management
iso9001.description: Consistent products and services and satisfied customers.

iso27001.name: ISO/IEC 27001 Information security
iso27001.description: Protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information.

iso14001.name: ISO 14001 Environmental management
iso14001.description: Control your environmental aspects and improve your environmental performance.

iso42001.name: ISO/IEC 42001 AI management
iso42001.description: Develop, provide or use AI systems responsibly.

iso45001.name: ISO 45001 Occupational health and safety
iso45001.description: Prevent work-related injury and ill health.

gdpr.name: GDPR
gdpr.description: Process personal data lawfully, fairly and securely.

eu_ai_act.name: EU AI Act
eu_ai_act.description: Obligations for AI systems placed on the market or used in the EU.

nis2.name: NIS2
nis2.description: Cybersecurity risk management for essential and important entities.

provider.name: Provider
provider.description: You develop AI systems, or have them developed, and place them on the market under your name.

deployer.name: Deployer
deployer.description: You use AI systems in your own work, for example a chatbot or a screening tool.

provider_and_deployer.name: Provider and deployer
provider_and_deployer.description: You build AI systems and also use AI systems in your own operations.

importer.name: Importer
importer.description: You bring AI systems from providers outside the EU onto the EU market.

distributor.name: Distributor
distributor.description: You make AI systems available on the EU market without being their provider or importer.

authorised_representative.name: Authorised representative
authorised_representative.description: A provider outside the EU has appointed you in writing to handle its AI Act duties on its behalf.

product_manufacturer.name: Product manufacturer
product_manufacturer.description: You sell products under your own name that contain a high-risk AI system as a safety component, so you carry the provider's duties.

not_applicable.name: Not in scope
not_applicable.description: You neither provide nor use AI systems that the AI Act covers.

unknown.name: Not sure yet
unknown.description: Pick this for now; the AI governance module helps you find out.

settings.title: Modules
settings.subtitle: Turn on the parts of CoreFlow your organisation needs. Turning a module off keeps its data.
settings.askFitPrompt: Look at our organisation profile and the modules we use today ({{ modules }}). Which other modules should we turn on, and why? Answer in short points.

empty.title: No modules yet
empty.body: Modules appear here as they become available. Each one supports one or more frameworks, such as ISO 9001 or GDPR.

settings.count: Showing {{ shown }} of {{ total }} modules, {{ enabled }} turned on.
settings.disableBody: {{ module }} disappears from the menu for everyone in this organisation. Its records are kept and come back when you turn it on again.

errors.dependencyDisabled: {{ module }} needs {{ modules }}. Turn that on first.
errors.requiredBy: {{ module }} is used by {{ modules }}. Turn those off first.
errors.alwaysOn: {{ module }} is always on and can't be turned off.
errors.unknown: That module doesn't exist any more. Reload the page.

settings.scopeGap: {{framework}} is in scope, but {{module}} is switched off.

profile.title: Organisation profile
profile.subtitle: Who you are and what you work towards. CoreFlow uses this to recommend modules and to give better answers.
profile.askAiRolePrompt: We are an organisation in the industry "{{ industry }}" and have chosen the AI Act role "{{ role }}". Explain in plain language what this role means, which obligations typically follow, and how we can check that the role is right.
profile.aiActRole: Role under the EU AI Act
profile.noTargets: No certification targets yet. Add one if you plan to get certified.
profile.noSites: No sites yet. Add the offices, plants or other locations your management system covers.

errors.countries: Use two-letter country codes separated by commas, for example NO, SE.
errors.site: A site needs a name and a two-letter country code.
errors.save: The profile could not be saved. Check the fields and try again.

profile.standardOn: Switched on in Standards and requirements
profile.standardOff: Switches on in Standards and requirements when you save
profile.standardUnavailable: Not in the requirement catalogue yet
profile.frameworksSync: The standards you tick here are switched on in Standards and requirements, and unticked ones are switched off.
profile.certificatesLive: Targets are plans. Certificates you hold (number, valid until, next surveillance audit) are kept under Audits.
profile.scopeBody: The description above is not the scope. Write the scope statement, with any exclusions and why, under Context.

terminology.title: Terminology
terminology.subtitle: Use the words your organisation already uses. Leave a field empty to keep the default.
terminology.askSuggestPrompt: Suggest terminology for our organisation based on our profile: which words should we use instead of deviation, document, risk, audit, finding, process, task, objective, incident, supplier and employee? Give singular and plural forms in English and Norwegian, and keep the defaults where they already fit.
terminology.preview: Your dashboard shows open {{ term.deviations }}, {{ term.documents }} awaiting review and overdue {{ term.tasks }}.

errors.incomplete: Fill in both the singular and the plural for a language, or leave both empty.
errors.unknownTerm: One of the terms isn't supported any more. Reload the page and try again.

terminology.resetBody: Every term goes back to the default wording, in every language.
terminology.savedToast: The terminology is saved and applied.
terminology.resetToast: The terminology is back to the defaults.

setup.title: Set up your organisation
setup.subtitle: A few short steps to tailor CoreFlow to how you work. You can come back and change everything later.
setup.rerunNotice: Setup was completed on {{ date }}. Running it again only turns modules on; nothing is turned off.

profile.title: Tell us about your organisation
profile.body: Industry, size and countries help CoreFlow suggest what is relevant to you.

frameworks.title: Which frameworks are in scope?
frameworks.body: Pick the standards and regulations you work towards, now or soon.
frameworks.hint: Not sure? Start with the one you need first. You can add more at any time under Settings, Organisation profile.

modules.title: Recommended modules
modules.body: Based on your frameworks, these modules cover what the standards ask for. Untick anything you don't need yet.
modules.askWhyPrompt: We chose these frameworks: {{ frameworks }}. Industry: {{ industry }}. Size: {{ size }}. CoreFlow recommends these modules: {{ modules }}. Explain briefly why each module matters for our frameworks, and which ones we could leave for later.
modules.empty: No modules to recommend yet. Pick a framework first, or carry on: you can turn modules on later.

roles.title: Who does what?
roles.body: CoreFlow gives each role sensible access. Invite your colleagues and give them the roles that match their responsibilities.

tasks.title: Your first tasks
tasks.body: Start with a short list of tasks so the work gets going. They show up in My Work.
tasks.unavailable: Tasks aren't available yet in this installation, so this step is skipped. You can carry on.
tasks.created: Tasks created: {{ count }}. You find them in My Work.
tasks.failed: The tasks could not be created. You can try again or skip this step.

reviewProfile.title: Check the organisation profile
reviewProfile.description: Make sure industry, sites, frameworks and certification targets are right.

inviteTeam.title: Invite your team
inviteTeam.description: Invite the people who will work in CoreFlow and give them roles.

policy.title: Publish the management system policy
policy.description: Upload or write the policy and send it for approval.

applicability.title: Decide which requirements apply
applicability.description: Go through the standards workspace and mark what applies to you.

deviations.title: Show the team how to report a deviation
deviations.description: Agree on the deviation types and register the first one together.

risk.title: Run the first risk assessment
risk.description: List the main risks and opportunities and agree on treatment.

audit.title: Plan the first internal audit
audit.description: Choose the scope, the auditors and a date.

done.title: Ready to go
done.body: Finish setup to see the result and make your first document.
done.summary: These modules will be turned on: {{ modules }}.
done.summaryNone: No new modules will be turned on.
done.journeyBody: A journey takes you step by step from the first scope statement to being ready for an audit. Each step says what to do and which requirements it covers.
done.journeyFailed: Could not start the journey. Try again from the standard's page.
done.created: Added: {{ policies }} policies, {{ risks }} risks and {{ ropa }} processing activities.
done.firstDocBody: Under Documents and reports you make finished documents from what you have entered, as Word or PDF.
done.targetLabel: When do you want to be ready for the audit?
done.targetHint: The journey then shows whether you are on track.

errors.unknownModules: One of the chosen modules no longer exists. Go back and check the list.
errors.recommendations: The recommendations could not be loaded. Please try again.

lookup.label: Organisation number
lookup.hint: Optional. We fetch industry, number of employees and country from the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities.
lookup.found: Found {{ name }}. Industry, size and country are filled in. Check that they are right.
lookup.unavailable: The register could not be reached. Fill in the fields yourself.

policies.title: Add policies
policies.body: Ready-made policies in plain words. Tick the ones you want. You can edit the text and send them for approval afterwards.

risks.title: Add risks
risks.body: Common risks for a business like yours. Tick the ones that apply to you. You assess and treat them afterwards.

ropa.title: Add processing activities
ropa.body: Typical ways a business processes personal data (the record of processing activities). Tick the ones you do.

starters.hint: They are added as drafts that you own. Nothing is shared or approved yet.
starters.failed: Some could not be added. You can add them later.

banner.title: Finish setting up your organisation
banner.body: A short wizard helps you choose frameworks, turn on the right modules and get the first tasks going.

industry.help: In your own words, for example "food production" or "IT consulting".

countries.help: Pick from the list. Laws and regulators depend on where you operate.

description.help: What you do, for whom and where. A few sentences are enough.

frameworks.help: The frameworks decide which requirements and modules CoreFlow suggests.

aiActRole.help: Providers build AI systems; deployers use them. Many organisations are deployers without knowing it.

targets.help: A target date makes the plan concrete and helps you schedule audits and reviews.

sites.help: List the locations your management system covers. It shapes the scope statement.

packages.title: Pick a package
packages.coverage: You have {{ on }} of {{ total }} areas on.

internal_control.name: Internal control / HSE
internal_control.description: Health, safety and environment: deviations, risk, training and the HSE handbook.

quality.name: Quality ISO 9001
quality.description: Documents, deviations, risk, internal audits and management review for ISO 9001.

security_privacy.name: Information security + privacy
security_privacy.description: ISO 27001 and GDPR: assets, risk, processing activities, audits and review.

full.name: Full management system
full.description: Every area switched on. Best when you already know CoreFlow.

packages.sectionBody: Switch on a whole package at once. Nothing is switched off.
packages.applyFailed: The package could not be switched on. Try again.
